title: Capacity Hedging & Burst Orchestration — Q3 Initiative and Release Ramp
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Deliver a Q3 pilot that reduces tail latency incidents during demand spikes by combining a lightweight hedging layer (short-term reserved buffers) with a burst orchestration policy that transparently routes to compatible model variants and capacity tiers. Scope includes API-level routing rules, console controls for hedge buckets, telemetry plumbing, and a canary rollout path. Out of scope: permanent pricing changes and marketplace integrations. Rationale: several customers hit unacceptable latency during synchronized launches; existing autoscale triggers are too slow for minute-level spikes. This initiative favors fast-failover and cost-bounded burst behavior over aggressive permanent reservation to balance unit economics.
metrics: P95 latency during spikes < 250ms for 95% of requests
Reduce incidents labeled "capacity-tail" by 60% in pilot tenants
Additional on-demand cost during spikes < 18% of baseline spend
milestones: 2025-07-24: API routing and policy PRD published (Confluence)
2025-08-21: Telemetry and dashboard widgets for hedging live
2025-09-18: Collect 2 weeks of canary metrics and safety review
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged backend + console toggle. Phase 1: Internal canary (infra team). Phase 2: 3 external pilot customers (opt-in). Phase 3: Gradual expansion with automatic rollback on error budget breach. Rollback criteria: >3severe latency regressions in 24h or cost > 30% over baseline for pilot tenants.
risks: Hedging increases short-term spend if spike prediction is poor
Model variant fallbacks could change output quality for some prompts
Complexity in billing attribution for burst usage
Operators may over-provision hedge buckets without guardrails
acceptance_criteria: APIs and console controls available behind flag
Canary completed with metrics meeting success thresholds
Runbook and rollback playbook documented and tested
Dashboard shows cost breakdown and P95/P99 during spikes
